findings.title: Provider thread outlives deadline and semaphore slot
findings.problem: provision_global_user runs service.get_or_create_customer_with_budget via asyncio.to_thread. When provision_default_budgets' wait_for fires at 8s, the coroutine is cancelled but the worker thread keeps blocking in the provider call, and the semaphore slot is released. Existing test only asserts the slot is freed, not that the work stopped.
findings.impact: PROVISION_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY bounds coroutines, not real provider calls. With a hung or slow proxy, bursts of first logins accumulate blocked threads in the default executor and can starve other to_thread users. Reachability depends on whether the LiteLLM client enforces its own timeout, which was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit client timeout to get_or_create_customer_with_budget, or hold the semaphore until the worker thread finishes, so hung calls cannot accumulate.
findings.check_notes: budget_service.py _call_provider_holding_slot acquires semaphore, runs provider as shielded task, releases in done callback; deadline cancel no longer frees slot early.

fix.change: Semaphore slot is now held until the provider task itself finishes (shielded task releases it on completion), so a deadline cancel no longer frees a slot while the worker thread still runs

findings.title: Missing LiteLLM service warns on every creation
findings.problem: The adapter returns None quietly (debug) when get_litellm_service_or_none() is None, but _provision_category logs logger.warning default_budget_provision_unavailable for every None result, so service-missing and empty-customer outcomes are indistinguishable. AC2 requires nothing above debug when the LiteLLM service is missing. No BudgetService-level test covers the log level.
findings.impact: Deployments with budget enforcement configured but no LiteLLM service emit one warning per category on every user creation across all five paths, violating AC2. Reachability of a registered litellm provider with a missing service was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Log provider-unavailable at debug and keep warning only for a real failed get_or_create (e.g. adapter signals unavailability separately); add a BudgetService test asserting no warning when the service is missing.
findings.check_notes: Adapter raises BudgetProviderUnavailableError when service missing; _provision_category logs debug and returns; warning kept only for None result.

fix.change: Adapter raises BudgetProviderUnavailableError when the LiteLLM service is missing; BudgetService logs it at debug and keeps warning only for a None customer result

findings.title: Sync DB session held during blocking provisioning
findings.problem: verify_email_and_login calls run_coroutine_blocking(provision_default_budgets, timeout=10s) inside the with get_session() block after session.commit(). The session and its pooled connection stay checked out for the whole remote provider call, though nothing after it needs the session (values were extracted before commit).
findings.impact: With a slow or down budget proxy each email verification pins a pooled connection for up to 10s; concurrent verifications can exhaust the sync pool and stall unrelated requests.
findings.recommendation: Extract user_id, user_email and user_username inside the with block, exit it, then run the provisioning call and generate the access token outside the session.
findings.check_notes: registration_service.py verify_email_and_login exits get_session after commit; provisioning and token generation run outside the session.

fix.change: verify_email_and_login exits the get_session block after commit, then provisions and mints the token outside the session

final_round.rationale: AC2 fails: a missing LiteLLM service logs a warning per category on every user creation, and two fragility issues (sync DB session held during provisioning; provider thread outliving the deadline) were confirmed in code. All four lenses and standards ran with no coverage gap; 16 candidates were dismissed as noise or by-design, 0 deferred. The provider-contract keyword naming deviation (budget_category vs spec category) was dismissed as internally consistent, and the two reachability-uncertain findings are capped at major.
